List.title: IFB/DCP/DPR/2609-1270095/Urban Forest Master Plan (UFMP)

Detail.description:
The Urban Forest Master Plan (UFMP) project is a City of Atlanta initiative to develop a 15-year strategic plan for protecting, managing, and expanding the City's urban forest and tree canopy. The plan will address Atlanta's goal of increasing canopy coverage to 50%, reversing recent canopy loss, improving equitable access to trees and nature, and strengthening the City's approach to tree planting, maintenance, natural-area management, and preservation.

The selected Consultant will conduct urban forest data and condition assessments, review City policies and practices, evaluate staffing and resource needs, and develop actionable recommendations for long-term urban forest management. A major component will be extensive community and stakeholder engagement, including public meetings, surveys, focus groups, Neighborhood Planning Unit presentations, stakeholder interviews, and a neighborhood ambassador program.

The final UFMP will provide specific goals, policies, benchmarks, funding strategies, implementation timelines, responsible parties, and performance measures to guide the City's urban forestry efforts through 2042. The project is expected to begin in Spring 2027 and must be completed by April 30, 2029.

List.title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL FOR SPANISH INTERPRETER FOR WINDER MUNICIPAL COURT

Detail.description:
PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF SERVICES
Description: A court interpreter is appointed to provide interpreting services for Court proceedings whenever 
the Court determines that the defendant cannot understand the English language and is incapable of being 
understood by the Court or counsel. The court interpreter is responsible for the accurate translation of verbal 
and written communication from Spanish to English and vice versa. Work will be performed at the Winder 
Community Center in Winder, Georgia. 
The City of Winder Municipal Court determines interpreter fees which are paid from the City's General Fund. 
The Office of the Court Clerk contracts for foreign language and sign interpreters when required. Currently, 
there is a need for one Spanish interpreter to be present during most scheduled court session. Court is held 
each Friday of the month with the exception of holidays. The court schedule for 2026 is included in Appendix 
A. This schedule is provided for example only, as dates may be subject to change at the City's discretion. The 
City of Winder Municipal Court is held at the Winder Community Center 113 E. Athens St., Winder, 
Georgia 30680 each Friday at 8 am- 12pm.
Qualifications: The qualifications for a court interpreter include strong command of the English and Spanish 
languages, including familiarity of legal terminology. The interpreter must also be able to translate the most 
formal dialogue to the most casual dialogue, including slang. The interpreter's vocabulary must consist of 
considerable depth in order to support the extent of subject matter, which is part of the judicial process. The 
interpreter must also be able to translate simultaneously at speaking rates of 200 words or more per minute.

List.title: REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS FOR CITY PROSECUTOR

Detail.description:
PURPOSE AND SCOPE OF SERVICES
A. Description: The City Solicitor performs advanced professional legal work involving the
prosecution of suspects in misdemeanor criminal cases and participates in administrative and
research functions in civil areas when directed. The Solicitor will prosecute cases within the
jurisdiction of the City Charter, ordinances, and Georgia State Statutes that are within the original
jurisdiction of the Winder Municipal Court.
B. Qualifications:
Education and Experience: Minimum qualifications include a Juris Doctorate degree from an
accredited law school, license to practice law in the state of Georgia, membership in the Georgia
State Bar Associations, and three (3) years experience as a practicing attorney.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Knowledge of proper courtroom procedure and the rules of
evidence; working knowledge of criminal law; working knowledge of local ordinances, laws, and
procedures; skill in basic supervisory principles and practices; ability to grasp complex factual
data, draw appropriate conclusions, and an ability to communicate complex legal ideas to a variety
of audiences in clear, comprehensive and professional manner; the ability to read, interpret, apply
and explain codes, rules, regulations, policies and procedures; ability to establish and maintain
effective working relationships with the City Administration, City Council, Municipal Judge,
Police Department, Court staff, and the general public

List.title: JWSC RFP 27-002 Progressive Design-Build Services for N Mainland WPCF Construction and Commissioning
List.agencyName: Brunswick-Glynn County Joint Water & Sewer Commiss

Detail.description:
Brunswick-Glynn County Joint Water & Sewer Commission is requesting Proposals for the design and construction of the following Project: Progressive Design Build Services for the North Mainland Water Pollution Control Facility Construction and Commissioning. 

Proposals for the construction of the Project will be received at 1703 Gloucester Street, Brunswick, Georgia 31520, until Thursday, October 29, 2026, at 12:00 NOON EST. 

To meet its future wastewater treatment needs, the BGJWSC plans to add a new water pollution control facility (North Mainland WPCF) on undeveloped property near Exit 42 along Interstate 95 in Glynn County, Georgia to provide additional treatment capacity to meet current and future system demands.

Due to rapid residential growth in the area and the potential for industrial development in the proposed sewershed, the selected Design-Builder will be required to plan for future expansions and include key infrastructure in the design and construction of the new WPCF to allow future treatment capacity to be easily added.

The Project will meet the BGJWSC's objectives of ensuring adequate treatment capacity and complying with regulations and water quality goals. Potential project components include: construction of a new Water Pollution Control Facility on the BGJWSC's property, offsite effluent discharge piping extension to the receiving water, extension of approximately 2,000 linear feet of gravity sewer to the proposed plant site, and connection of existing upstream force mains to the gravity sewer system that feeds the plant site. 

The Project will include the planning, evaluation, design, construction, commissioning, and startup necessary to place the Project in full operation according to contract requirements. 

The Project is to be designed and constructed using the progressive design-build delivery method.

Detail.description:
Pursuant to the State Purchasing Act (O.C.G.A. §§ 50-5-50 et seq.), the University of Georgia (UGA) is issuing this Request for Quotes (RFQ) to establish an agency contract with a qualified supplier for the supply, delivery, and cylinder/dewar float management of Liquid & Gaseous Helium, Liquid & Gaseous Nitrogen, and Industrial Dry Ice Pellets.
Bidders shall provide firm, itemized pricing covering all product categories, purities, container sizes, and pressure ratings specified in the Bid Specification. Detail.description:
The City of Atlanta, on behalf of the Department of Watershed Management, will shortly undergo a Multi-Step 
Sealed Bid process comprised of a prequalification phase as the initial step, followed by an Invitation for Bids for 
the procurement of qualified suppliers to provide maintenance services for permeable pavers. The work includes 
operations and maintenance of approximately four miles of permeable paver streets, quarterly surface sweeping 
using a regenerative air vacuum, and repair of underground infrastructure as needed. Interested vendors during the prequalification phase will be evaluated based on their demonstrated experience with the installation and 
maintenance of permeable paver streets, regenerative air vacuum sweeping, and underground infrastructure repairs. Vendors must demonstrate a minimum of five years of relevant experience, provide an organizational chart and resumes for key project personnel, and identify two completed or current projects within the last two years that are similar in scope and complexity. Vendors must also demonstrate an established safety program and provide the required safety record information. The City's expectation is that the selected supplier will provide safe, effective, and responsive maintenance services that support the continued performance and condition of the City's permeable paver infrastructure. Services may include regenerative air vacuum sweeping, vegetation removal, replacement and resetting of pavers, drainage inspections and cleaning, repairs to sinkholes and depressions, stormwater structure repairs, and sewer, water, and other infrastructure repairs as required. A Pre-Solicitation Conference will be noticed and held to provide additional details and answer questions from interested vendors. We look forward to your participation.

List.title: CP3571 UGA CM@R: South Milledge Roundabouts

Detail.description:
The Board of Regents of the University System of Georgia ('BOR') as 'Owner', on behalf of the University of Georgia, 'User' is soliciting Statements of Qualifications from firms interested in providing construction management at-risk services for the construction of a project known as "Project No. CP 3571 South Milledge Roundabouts" at the University of Georgia, Athens, Georgia.
Project Background
South Milledge Avenue is a two-lane corridor with increasing traffic volumes due to evolving land uses. Posted speed limits are 40 mph in the Track/Turner project area, increasing to 50 mph at the State Botanical Garden (SBG) project area. The roundabouts are intended to improve vehicular safety and operations for turning movements into/out of the venues while preserving through movement on South Milledge, and to improve pedestrian safety (including safe crossing between the Track & Field and Turner complexes to support shared parking during major events). The design will incorporate sidewalks, crosswalks, and pedestrian refuge islands; and include associated improvements such as stormwater management, utility relocations, lighting, signage, and landscaping. Both roundabouts are envisioned to be similar in size and scale to the existing roundabout at South Milledge and Whitehall Road.
 
This South Milledge Avenue Roundabouts project is within the Athens-Clarke County (ACC) roadway right-of-way/easement, with the Georgia Department of Transportation (GDOT) and ACC having jurisdictional responsibilities for the corridor. The roundabout construction project will be delivered in coordination with GDOT/ACC requirements adjacent to Board of Regents property.
Project Description
The Project includes a coordinated two-roundabout program along South Milledge Avenue.
1. Detail.description:
This Request for Quotes (RFQ or Sourcing Event) is being issued to establish a contract with a qualified supplier who will meet the State Entity's needs as described in this Sourcing Event. This RFQ process will be conducted to gather and evaluate responses from supplier for potential award. All qualified suppliers are invited to participate by submitting responses, as further defined below. After evaluating all suppliers' responses received prior to the closing date of this Sourcing Event and resolution of any contract exceptions, the preliminary results of the RFQ process will be publicly announced, including the names of all participating suppliers and the evaluation results. Subject to the protest process, final contract award(s) will be publicly announced thereafter.
The scope of work for this project will include the replacement of the dual duct terminal units on the ground floor,1st floor, and 2nd floor of the CH Building. Only the terminal units that have not been part of recent renovations willbe replaced. The temperature sensors associated with these units will be replaced as well. The contractor willdemolish and replace ductwork connected to the terminal units and duct mains as needed to replace terminal units.The scope also includes any remaining pneumatic controls to be replaced with electronic controls. Detail.description:
The Bulloch County Board of Commissioners is accepting sealed bids from GDOT Prequalified Contractors for this project: FY27-ENGCP-002-1 S&S Greenway Phase 3 Project (Federal Aid) & Josh Hagin Road Paving Project. The project consists of extending a Shared Use Path, known as the S&S Greenway, to approximately 1.96 miles from its existing terminus at the Five Points Roundabout at Pretoria Rushing Road and Burkhalter Road to its new proposed terminus at Grimshaw Road. The S&S Greenway extension project begins near latitude 32.410364 and longitude -81.731016 and the project ends near latitude 32.399169 and longitude -81.698229. The Josh Hagin Road project begins near latitude 32.409231 and longitude -81.729019 and the project ends near latitude 32.399349 and longitude -81.698624.

All contractors seeking to provide construction delivery services to Bulloch County for this project shall submit evidence of current active approval as a GDOT Prequalified Contractor as of the bid submission deadline November 13, 2026, 3:00 PM EST, as it appears on GDOT's Directory of Prequalified Contractors webpage.

List.title: Debris Management Monitoring Services

Detail.description:
SCOPE OF WORK 
Disaster Debris Monitoring Services 
The selected firm will be expected to provide disaster debris monitoring services to include debris generated from the public rights-of-way, private property, drainage areas, waterways, and other public, eligible or designated areas. Services may include but are not limited to: 
a. Prepare and submit daily operational reports to the City no later than 10:00am the following day,
including debris quantities, collection areas, contractor activity, staffing, operational issies, and progress to date. 
b. Scheduling work for all team members and contractors on a daily basis.
c. Hiring, training, scheduling, and managing field staff.
d. Monitoring recovery contractor operations and making/implementing recommendations to improve efficiency as well as speed up recovery work and assure all debris removal work meets FEMA eligibility guidelines.
e. Certifying contractor vehicles for debris removal using methodology and documentation practices appropriate for contract monitoring.
f. Entering load tickets into a database application.
g. Digitizing of source documentation (such as load tickets).
h. Furnishing and operating an automated/electronic (paperless) debris tracking system.
i. Developing daily operational reports to keep the City informed of work progress.
j. Develop and maintain maps, GIS applications, dashboards, and other visual reporting tools, as necessary, to track debris collection, monitor contractor progress, identify completed and outstanding collection areas, provide the City with current operational information, and ensure compliance with applicable EHP and FEMA guidelines.
k. Comprehensive review, reconciliation, and validation of debris removal contractor(s) invoices prior to submission of the City for processing.

MACON WATER AUTHORITY MACON, GEORGIA

List.title: Stormwater Program Management

Detail.description:
The City of Byron (City) is seeking proposals from qualified firms, contractors, and/or joint ventures interested in providing administration, engineering and inspection, and construction services for a project known as Stormwater Program Management (the Project). The City desires to select a qualified firm, contractor, or joint venture team to operate and manage its Stormwater Program. The selected team will be responsible for administrative, engineering and inspection, and construction services for daily and routine assistance with operation and management of the City's Stormwater Program. The City's Stormwater Department is responsible for operation and maintenance of approximately 550 stormwater structures, approximately 16 miles of stormwater pipes and culverts, countless miles of ditches and drainage easements, and 57 stormwater management facilities. The City's watershed is comprised of five basins, having ten contributing outfalls. The City's Stormwater Department is responsible for operation and management of its Stormwater Utility. Due to factors beyond the City's control, the City is seeking to contract with a firm, contractor, or team to assist with operating and managing its Stormwater Program for a duration of three years with the ability to add up to two additional years based on performance. The annual budget for the Project is approximately $250,000. 
Sealed proposals for 'Stormwater Program Management' will be received by the City of Byron Purchasing Department located at the Byron Municipal Complex, 401 Main Street, Byron, Georgia 31008 until 10:00 AM, Thursday, November 19, 2026.

List.title: B2432 - Chattahoochee River Trail, Phase II

Detail.description:
The Chattahoochee River Trail was included in the 2018 Cobb County Greenways & Trails Master
Plan as a priority project and detailed in the Chattahoochee RiverLands Greenway Study, a regional river corridor plan for the 100-mile Chattahoochee River corridor. One task of this study was to develop a pilot project conceptual plan for a multi-use path on Cobb County-owned property between SR 139/Mableton Parkway and SR 8/US 278/Veterans Memorial Highway. The conceptual
plan was adopted by the Cobb County Board of Commissioners on June 23, 2020 and provides
unprecedented access to the portion of the Chattahoochee River south of I-285, giving people the opportunity to see, interact with, and experience nature in a new and unique way, while also
serving as a model for implementation of future RiverLand segments.
Phase II of the subject project proposes to provide paved paths for shared use by pedestrians and
bicycles along the Chattahoochee River between SR 139/Mableton Parkway and Nickajack Creek. In
addition, this phase includes a bridge over a small creek at the southern end of the project and
boardwalks over environmentally sensitive areas. The logical termini will be SR 139/Mableton
Parkway at Lee Industrial Boulevard on the southern end, where it will connect to an existing 10- foot wide shared-use path, and Nickajack Creek on the northern end. Nickajack Creek is also the
southern terminus for Phase I.

List.title: REQUEST FOR QUALIFICATIONS FOR ARCHITECTS, STRUCTURAL ENGINEERS, AND SURVEYORS FOR CONSTRUCTION

Detail.description: The City of Newnan has been awarded $4.6 million through a Congressionally Directed Spending allocation in the FY2023 Federal Budget. The Newnan City Council has authorized the Newnan Urban Redevelopment Agency (NURA) to serve as the administrator of these funds. The program includes two primary activities: the rehabilitation of owner-occupied housing units and the construction of new homes on City-owned lots. These new homes will be sold to low-, moderate-, and middle-income families whose household income is at or below 120% of the Area Median Income (AMI) for Coweta County. To support this initiative, NURA is seeking Statements of Qualifications from experienced and licensed architectural, structural engineering, and land surveying firms. The purpose of this RFQ is to establish a pre-qualified pool of firms that can provide professional services for the planning, design, and implementation of both new home construction and residential rehabilitation projects. Selected firms may be engaged on an as-needed basis for tasks such as: Site surveys and platting, Structural assessments and design, Architectural drawings and construction documents, Code compliance reviews, Construction phase support. This RFQ process will enable NURA to expedite professional service contracting while ensuring a high standard of quality and compliance with federal funding requirements. NURA reserves the right to reject any or all responses determined not to be in the best interest of the program.

The activities in this program involve the rehabilitation owner occupied housing units and the construction of new homes on City of Newnan owned properties. The new construction housing units will be sold to low-, moderate- and middle-income families whose household income is at or below 120% of the area median income for the county in which the property is located. The NURA is looking to engage qualified general contractors to construct new homes on or perform various repairs and rehabilitation of these properties. This solicitation is designed to enable the NURA to develop a pool of qualified contractors. This list/plan will be distributed to the contractors in the pool for the purpose of soliciting bids for performing the rehabilitation/new construction. The NURA will award the contract to the lowest bid that is both responsive and responsible. The NURA reserves the right to reject any or all responses not deemed acceptable.
